reply: You can register for Self Assessment on the HMRC website. Here’s the link to get started: [Register for Self Assessment](https://www.gov.uk/register-for-self-assessment). Make sure to complete your registration by 5 October after the end of the tax year in which you started your self-employment. If you need further assistance, feel free to ask!

sources.title: Register for Self Assessment
sources.excerpt: If you need to send a tax return and are not already registered, you must register for Self Assessment. New sole traders usually need to register by 5 October after the end of the tax year in which they started.

sources.title: Register as self-employed
sources.excerpt: If you start working for yourself you need to register with HMRC for Self Assessment and for National Insurance. New sole traders usually need to register by 5 October after the end of the tax year in which self-employment began.

sources.title: VAT registration timing — rolling 12 months and 30-day forward look
sources.excerpt: Rolling 12-month (backward) test: if at the end of any month your taxable supplies in the previous 12 months (or less) exceed £90,000, you must notify HMRC within 30 days of that month-end. Effective date of registration is typically the first day of the second month after you went over the threshold. Forward-looking 30-day test: if at any time you expect taxable supplies in the next 30 days alone to exceed £90,000, you must register by the end of that 30-day period; the effective date is the date you first formed that expectation. These are separate tests — do not confuse an 11-month build-up plus next month with the forward look. Always confirm on GOV.UK / VAT Notice 700/1.
